examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the MuleSoft Integration Foundations exam?
examDifficulty.summary: This entry-level exam focuses on integration concepts and terminology rather than building a complete Mule application. Learn what each part of Anypoint Platform does and how APIs can be organized for reuse.
bullets: 40 scored questions in 70 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
70% to pass, which is 28 correct answers out of 40.
Concepts before coding: Recognize the purpose of API-led layers, platform tools, and basic Mule application parts.
No prior MuleSoft experience is required. General IT knowledge and the recommended learning materials provide a starting point.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Complete the MuleSoft Integration Foundations Trailhead learning and explain API-led connectivity in your own words. Aim for at least 80% on practice questions and review any terms you cannot define clearly.

examFormat.heading: MuleSoft Integration Foundations exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. It tests basic integration concepts and Anypoint Platform tools.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Some questions describe an integration requirement and ask which API-led layer or Anypoint tool would fit.
bestWayToPass: Learn the API-led layers: System APIs connect to systems of record, Process APIs combine data or apply business logic, and Experience APIs tailor data for a consumer.
Match platform tools to their jobs: Studio builds Mule applications, Exchange catalogs assets, API Manager applies API policies, and Runtime Manager deploys and monitors applications.
Compare integration patterns: Understand point-to-point, hub and spoke, ESB, and API-led approaches and their trade-offs.
Review Mule app basics: Learn how a flow starts, how messages move, and where DataWeave transformations fit.

certificationCard.description: This entry-level exam covers the basics of API-led connectivity, what each part of Anypoint Platform does, and the integration vocabulary you need to work on a MuleSoft project. The exam is 40 scored questions in 70 minutes, with a 70% pass mark, weighted towards Essential integration concepts and terminology (20%) and Technical complexities and patterns in integration development (18%).

blocks.heading: API-Led Connectivity and Anypoint Platform
blocks.body: API-led connectivity organizes integrations into reusable layers. A System API provides controlled access to a system of record. A Process API combines data or applies business rules. An Experience API presents data for a particular user experience or channel. Reuse means teams can build new solutions on existing APIs instead of creating a separate point-to-point connection each time. Anypoint Studio is used to build Mule applications, Exchange catalogs reusable assets, API Manager manages API policies, and Runtime Manager deploys and monitors applications.

blocks.heading: Mule Applications, Flows, and Messages
blocks.body: A Mule application contains flows that process messages. A source starts a flow, for example an HTTP listener or a scheduler. Processors then transform or route the message and may call connectors to reach other systems. A Mule event includes a payload and attributes. The payload holds the message content; attributes hold contextual information such as HTTP headers. Variables can hold additional values during processing.

blocks.heading: DataWeave and Connectors
blocks.body: DataWeave is MuleSoft’s language for transforming and mapping data between formats and structures. Connectors provide configured operations for specific systems and services. Teams can discover reusable connectors and other assets in Exchange. Use a connector to communicate with a supported system; use DataWeave to shape the data being exchanged.

blocks.heading: API Management and Deployment
blocks.body: API Manager applies policies and manages API access, such as requiring client credentials or setting usage limits. Runtime Manager deploys and monitors Mule applications. Applications can run in MuleSoft-managed cloud environments or in customer-managed infrastructure, depending on the deployment architecture. Runtime Fabric is an option for running Mule applications on customer-managed infrastructure while managing them through Anypoint Platform.

blocks.heading: Integration Patterns and Reuse
blocks.body: Point-to-point integrations connect systems directly and can become difficult to maintain as the number of systems and connections grows. Hub-and-spoke and ESB approaches centralize some integration functions. API-led connectivity organizes reusable APIs in layers so teams can expose system capabilities, compose processes, and serve different consumers. Choose a pattern based on reuse, governance, and the organization’s operating needs.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the MuleSoft Integration Foundations exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions ask what a platform component or integration pattern is used for. Identify the task, then select the API layer or tool that owns it.

blocks.heading: Compare Integration Patterns
blocks.body: Review point-to-point, hub and spoke, ESB, and API-led connectivity. Understand why direct connections become harder to maintain as systems are added.

blocks.heading: Know Each Anypoint Tool
blocks.body: Studio is for building, Exchange for discovering and sharing assets, API Manager for policies, and Runtime Manager for deployment and monitoring.

blocks.heading: Review API Basics
blocks.body: Understand what an API exposes, the broad difference between REST and SOAP, and how an API specification describes an interface.

blocks.heading: Recognize DataWeave
blocks.body: DataWeave transforms and maps data between structures and formats. Practice recognizing when data must be reshaped before it reaches a destination.

blocks.heading: Use Connectors and Exchange
blocks.body: Connectors provide operations for particular systems. Exchange helps teams discover and reuse connectors, APIs, and other assets.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Related credentials after MuleSoft Integration Foundations
nextCertsAfter.intro: Build on integration fundamentals with a role-focused MuleSoft developer or architect credential.

sampleQuestions.question: A team needs an API that reads customer records from SAP and hides SAP-specific details from other teams. Which API-led layer fits?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A System API provides a managed interface to a system of record such as SAP.
whyWrong: A Process API composes data or applies business rules across systems.
A reusable API provides a stable interface rather than requiring direct access.
An Experience API shapes data for a particular consumer or channel.

sampleQuestions.question: A mobile client needs a consumer-specific response while internal System and Process APIs remain behind the API boundary. Which API layer should shape that response?
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Experience API presents data in a form suited to one consumer, such as the mobile application, while using existing APIs behind it.
whyWrong: A System API provides access to a system of record rather than shaping the mobile experience.
A new database is unnecessary when existing APIs expose the required data.
A Process API combines data or applies business logic across systems.

sampleQuestions.question: Where can a team publish and discover reusable APIs and connectors?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Anypoint Exchange is the catalog for publishing and discovering reusable APIs, connectors, and other assets.
whyWrong: Studio is the development environment for Mule applications.
API Manager applies policies and manages API access.
Runtime Manager deploys and monitors applications.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool can require a client ID and set API call limits?
sampleQuestions.explanation: API Manager applies policies such as client access requirements and usage limits.
whyWrong: This is the platform tool for API policies and controls.
Studio is used to build Mule applications.
Exchange catalogs assets rather than enforcing runtime policies.

sampleQuestions.question: Many systems connect directly to each other, so changes frequently break integrations. What pattern is this, and what approach can improve reuse?
options: Hub and spoke, replaced by direct calls
sampleQuestions.explanation: Point-to-point links can multiply as systems are added; API-led connectivity can create reusable interfaces in layers.
whyWrong: API-led is the recommended reusable approach, not the problematic pattern described.
Direct connections do not address the growing number of dependencies.
Hub and spoke centralizes connections but is not the pattern identified here.

sampleQuestions.question: What starts a Mule flow?
options: A source such as an HTTP listener
sampleQuestions.explanation: A source, such as an HTTP listener or scheduler, receives or generates an event that starts the flow.
whyWrong: DataWeave transforms data after a flow starts.
An API policy controls access rather than creating the event that starts a flow.
A source such as a listener or scheduler starts the flow.

sampleQuestions.question: What is DataWeave used for?
sampleQuestions.explanation: DataWeave maps and transforms data between formats and structures.
whyWrong: DataWeave maps and transforms data between structures and formats.
Runtime Manager deploys and monitors applications.
Exchange catalogs APIs and reusable assets.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to run Mule applications in a MuleSoft-managed cloud environment. Which option fits?
sampleQuestions.explanation: CloudHub is MuleSoft’s managed cloud deployment option for Mule applications.
whyWrong: Studio is used to build the application, not to host it.
Exchange catalogs assets rather than running applications.
CloudHub is the managed deployment option described.

sampleQuestions.question: Which part of a Mule event carries context such as HTTP headers?
options: A variable set in the flow
sampleQuestions.explanation: Event attributes contain contextual information such as transport metadata and HTTP headers.
whyWrong: Attributes hold contextual information such as HTTP headers.
The payload contains the main message content.
Variables store flow values but are separate from event attributes.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants its Mule runtime to run on infrastructure it operates and still be managed through Anypoint Platform. Which deployment option supports this?
options: Anypoint Studio on a developer laptop
sampleQuestions.explanation: Runtime Fabric connects a customer-managed runtime environment to Anypoint Platform management.
whyWrong: Runtime Fabric supports customer-managed environments connected to Anypoint management.
Studio is a development tool, not the production runtime.
Exchange catalogs assets rather than hosting running applications.

sampleQuestions.question: Why does API-led connectivity encourage reuse?
options: It prevents teams from creating APIs
New projects can call existing APIs
It replaces every system with MuleSoft
It stores all enterprise data in one database
sampleQuestions.explanation: Teams can reuse existing APIs instead of rebuilding a separate connection for each new project.
whyWrong: API-led connectivity promotes reuse and does not forbid new APIs.
The approach connects systems rather than replacing them all.
It does not consolidate all enterprise data into one database.

sampleQuestions.question: At a high level, how do REST and SOAP commonly differ?
options: REST is only for databases and SOAP only for files
REST uses resources; SOAP uses XML and WSDL
sampleQuestions.explanation: REST commonly uses HTTP methods and resource representations; SOAP uses XML-based messages and commonly a WSDL service description.
whyWrong: REST and SOAP are distinct approaches to APIs.
SOAP is not newer than REST in this comparison.
Neither approach is limited to those data sources.

sampleQuestions.question: A flow should check a database for new orders every 15 minutes. What can start it on that schedule?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A scheduler source can trigger a flow on a configured schedule.
whyWrong: An HTTP listener responds to inbound requests rather than a timer.
API policies govern access and do not trigger scheduled work.
A scheduler source can start the flow on the configured interval.

sampleQuestions.question: Which statement about MuleSoft connectors is correct?
options: They remove the need for APIs
A connector must be written from scratch for each project
sampleQuestions.explanation: Connectors provide reusable operations for particular systems, and teams can discover them through Exchange.
whyWrong: Connectors can work with APIs and do not remove the need to design them.
MuleSoft connectors support many systems, not only Salesforce.
Prebuilt connectors can be reused rather than rebuilt for every project.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants different call limits for free and paid API consumers. What should it configure?
options: SLA tiers or policies in API Manager
A separate Mule application for each consumer
sampleQuestions.explanation: API Manager can apply policies or service-level tiers to set different access and usage limits.
whyWrong: DataWeave transforms data but does not enforce consumer call limits.
Exchange catalogs assets and does not enforce runtime usage limits.
Separate applications are unnecessary for this kind of access policy.
